title: Zip an already-started baby jacket
instruction: Use your left arm to pin the jacket down against the table so it stays still. While holding it down, use your right arm to grab the orange zipper pull and zip the jacket up to the collar. If it stops short, regrasp the orange pull and finish sliding it to the top stop. Let go once the zipper reaches the top.
context: Closing a garment zipper requires holding flexible fabric steady while guiding the pull along a narrow path.
setup: Lay a padded baby jacket front up, with sleeves extended and hem toward the arms. For a physical replica, use a woven polyester shell and lining with quilted polyester batting, about 8 mm thick overall when uncompressed. The jacket is about 240 mm long and 370 mm across the sleeves. Use a one-way, open-end separating jacket zipper with 180 mm of travel, molded acetal teeth, woven polyester tape, and a zinc-alloy non-locking slider with a bottom insertion pin and retaining box. Fit the slider with a custom orange PETG pull block, 3D-printed at a 0.2 mm layer height and 40% infill. The block measures 18 mm along the zipper, 16 mm across it, and 24 mm tall. Glue the block to the top of the zinc-alloy slider using J-B Weld PlasticBonder Tan (SKU 50133), a two-part urethane adhesive. Clean and lightly sand the mating faces, mix equal parts, and hold the block centered while it cures for at least one hour at room temperature. Use a rigid PETG spacer if needed to center the block about 36 mm above the tabletop. Keep the two side faces flat and accessible and keep the block, spacer, and adhesive clear of the teeth and tape. Start with the pin fully seated, the slider 20 mm up from the hem, and the orange block exposed. The zipper origin is at (145, 0) mm in the tabletop plane, with +x away from the arms and +y to robot-left.
scoring: Score the fraction of the remaining 160 mm of travel closed. Score zero if the pin protrudes more than 3 mm at any point. Award 1.0 if the slider is within 3 mm of the top and both gripper tool centers are more than 40 mm from the garment and zipper. Otherwise cap the score at 0.9625.
run_limit: 4,800 control steps (240 simulated seconds at 20 Hz)
reset_notes: Restore the documented starting arrangement and wait for cloth to settle before each run.
fidelity: The simulation represents the jacket shell, lining, and batting as one continuous deformable surface with a sewn hem bridge. The orange pull is an oversized solid 18 × 16 × 24 mm cuboid rigidly fixed to the slider. The matching physical attachment is a custom 3D-printed PETG block with 40% infill fixed to the real metal slider as specified in the setup. The wider, thicker grasp faces and fixed orientation make it easier to grasp than a typical thin, hinged zipper tab. Rigid internal rails approximate zipper travel. The visible teeth follow slider position, and the physics omits individual tooth meshing and cloth snags.
scores: Dream-1: 0.070686100050807 in 1200 steps. Scripted demo: 1.00 (raw 1.0) in 503 steps.
